cim: Coca-Cola Isn’t Leaving the Holidays to Artificial Intelligence This Year - media-marketing.com
cim_eredeti: Coca-Cola Isn’t Leaving the Holidays to Artificial Intelligence This Year - media-marketing.com
szoveg_eredeti:
Deep-frying a turkey, family meals and playing American football are among the scenes Coca-Cola has chosen for this year’s Christmas commercials. At first glance, these are familiar elements of the brand’s holiday repertoire. What sets the new Enjoy Joy spots apart from previous editions is how they were made. After two years of experimenting with generative artificial intelligence, Coca-Cola has returned to traditional film production for this campaign.

The previous two holiday seasons brought AI reinterpretations of the famous Holidays Are Coming commercial, including the recognizable trucks traveling through snowy landscapes. Although, according to earlier statements from the company, the ads exceeded internal performance benchmarks, they received mixed reactions from audiences, particularly because of the quality of the generated visuals and the decision to recreate one of the most recognizable Christmas advertising motifs using artificial intelligence.

This year’s creative decision therefore represents an interesting shift, but not a complete departure from AI technology for Coca-Cola. The new spots, developed in collaboration with WPP Open X, under the creative leadership of Ogilvy, were directed by Paul Dektor and produced by Mayan Productions.

Enjoy Joy features two versions of the film in which the holiday atmosphere is built not around spectacular scenes, but through situations that bring family and friends together. The spots have been produced in 30-, 15- and six-second formats and will run on television, streaming services, digital platforms and social media. Adapted versions have also been created for the Hispanic market.

The films are part of the broader Refresh Your Holidays campaign, launched last year, which this season also includes content designed for social media. Among these is the Grandma’s Holiday Table series, dedicated to grandparents and other family members who preserve holiday traditions. Through recipes, family stories and rituals passed down through generations, the series explores a side of the holidays that cannot be captured in just a few seconds of a television commercial.

Content creators will also participate in distributing the campaign across Meta, TikTok, Pinterest and YouTube, while a partnership with Amazon has been arranged for additional media and commerce integrations. The campaign will also appear in cinemas, audio formats and out-of-home advertising.

Another longstanding Coca-Cola Christmas tradition is continuing on the streets of American cities. This year’s holiday caravan has more than 270 planned stops, where visitors can take photos with Santa Claus and the recognizable polar bear mascot, participate in festive activities and receive gifts. In collaboration with USO, visitors at selected locations can also leave messages for members of the US armed forces and their families.

Christmas imagery is also returning to the packaging of Coca-Cola, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar and Diet Coke, while the seasonal flavors Coca-Cola Holiday Creamy Vanilla and its zero-sugar version will once again be available for a limited time. For a brand that has spent decades building its own Christmas iconography, this year’s return to traditional production is particularly interesting in the context of discussions about the role of AI in the creative industry.
